doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

title: Options for graduating jazz musicians and Girl from Ipanema
summary: Ricker says having many skills gives options, most jazz players teach, and the two joke about Girl from Ipanema requests.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: That’s fine. And the opportunities for graduating jazz musicians are obviously different than they were 20, 30 years ago.

Yeah. Well they weren’t great 20 or 30 years ago either. You know the thing I think is that if you’ve got many different things that you can do, and do at a high level, you can have more options, and that’s the name of the game, you know, having some options. And jazz people, I mean I’d say 95 percent of people who call themselves jazz musicians also teach. It’s just part of the deal you know. If you’re going to be a jazz guy they generally write tunes too. And you know, know how to orchestrate them. So there’d be many things you can do just in that area. Your writing helps your playing and your playing helps your writing. It all goes together.
And some of them still play “Girl from Ipanema” at dance gigs too.
It’s so funny that, “You guys know anything Latin?” If you get a request, 90 percent of the time it’s “Girl from Ipanema.”
Which has to have the strangest bridge of any tune, at least that I know.
